questions.stem: A 16-year-old, highly allergic girl who is stung by a bee gives herself a shot of epinephrine prescribed by her physician. Because epinephrine activates β-adrenergic receptors, it will relieve the effects of the bee sting by decreasing which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: The contraction of the airway smooth muscle

options.label: B
options.text: The strength of ventricular muscle contraction

options.label: C
options.text: The rate of depolarization in the SA node

options.label: D
options.text: The transport of calcium into skeletal muscle fibers

questions.answerText: The contraction of the airway smooth muscle
questions.solutionHtml:
The contraction of the airway smooth muscle
  • Epinephrine (adrenaline) to reduce the bee sting body's allergic response.
  • This is an example of Anaphylaxis: a generalized immune reaction of the body in the individuals sensitive to the agent that causes the body to enter into anaphylactic shock and puts the individual's life at immediate risk. This can be caused by agents such as toxins in insect bites, vaccines, antibiotics (such as penicillin), and even some foods such as Peanuts.
  • There is the release of inflammatory mediators such as Histamine. These cause bronchoconstriction and increased secretions in the airway leading to mortality.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 333, Goodman and Gilman’s The Pharmacological basis of Therapeutics,Edition-, Page number: 285.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman is seen by a neurologist to evaluate her incapacitating muscle weakness. The neurologist suspects myasthenia gravis and decides to confirm his diagnosis by administering a drug that increases the force of muscle contraction in patients with myasthenia gravis. Caution is advised when administering the drug to patients with heart disease because bradycardia may develop. Which of the following most likely explains the ability of the drug to increase the force of muscle contraction in patients with myasthenia gravis?

options.label: A
options.text: Increasing the amount of acetylcholine (ACh) released by a motoneurons

options.label: B
options.text: Increasing the affinity of the skeletal muscle acetylcholine receptors to acetylcholine

options.label: C
options.text: Increasing the motoneuron discharge rate

options.label: D
options.text: Decreasing the metabolic breakdown rate of acetylcholine

questions.answerText: Decreasing the metabolic breakdown rate of acetylcholine
questions.solutionHtml:
Decreasing the metabolic breakdown rate of acetylcholine
  • The drug used to test for myasthenia gravis is an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor such as Edrophonium.
  • The drug prevents the breakdown of acetylcholine, increasing the duration of time acetylcholine remains in the synaptic cleft
  • Because acetylcholine can bind to the end-plate receptors for a longer time, the magnitude of the end-plate potential increases, increasing the probability of it generating an action potential.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 118

questions.stem: Which of the following muscle proteins plays an important role in the contraction of both smooth and striated muscles?

options.label: A
options.text: Calmodulin

options.label: B
options.text: Troponin

options.label: C
options.text: Tropomyosin

options.label: D
options.text: Actin

questions.solutionHtml:
Actin

Actin plays an important role in the contraction of both smooth and striated muscles.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 69–70, 82–83

questions.stem: When comparing the contractile responses in smooth and skeletal muscle, which of the following is most different?

options.label: A
options.text: The source of activator calcium

options.label: B
options.text: The role of calcium in initiating contraction

options.label: C
options.text: The mechanism of force generation

options.label: D
options.text: The source of energy used during contraction

questions.answerText: The role of calcium in initiating contraction
questions.solutionHtml:
The role of calcium in initiating contraction

The greatest difference in excitation-contraction coupling between skeletal muscle and smooth muscle involves the role of calcium in initiating contraction.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 65, 84., Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page number 103,104.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding the action potential of skeletal muscle?

options.label: A
options.text: It spreads inward to all parts of the muscle via the T-tubules

options.label: B
options.text: It has a prolonged plateau phase

options.label: C
options.text: It causes the immediate uptake of Ca2+ into the lateral sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum

options.label: D
options.text: It is longer than the action potential of cardiac muscle

questions.answerText: It spreads inward to all parts of the muscle via the T-tubules
questions.solutionHtml:
It spreads inward to all parts of the muscle via the T-tubules

T-tubules are invaginations of the plasma membrane, which are present exclusively in striated muscle. Their role is to maintain the SR calcium store under the tight control of membrane depolarization via the voltage sensor channel DHPR.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 65–73, 78–80, 743.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true regarding the contractile response of skeletal muscle?

options.label: A
options.text: It starts after the action potential is over

options.label: B
options.text: It does not last as long as the action potential

options.label: C
options.text: It produces more tension when the muscle contracts isometrically than isotonically

options.label: D
options.text: It produces more tension when the muscle contracts isotonically than isometrically

questions.answerText: It produces more tension when the muscle contracts isometrically than isotonically
questions.solutionHtml:
It produces more tension when the muscle contracts isometrically than isotonically

Skeletal muscle produces more tension when the muscle contracts isometrically than isotonically. Isometric contractions involve sarcomere shortening and increasing muscle tension.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 58–71.

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics is the most similar between the capillaries in the skeletal muscle and pulmonary circulations?

options.label: A
options.text: The interstitial protein concentration

options.label: B
options.text: The interstitial hydrostatic pressure

options.label: C
options.text: The capillary oncotic pressure

options.label: D
options.text: The capillary hydrostatic pressure

questions.solutionHtml:
The capillary oncotic pressure

Blood flows in series through the systemic and pulmonary circulations, and, therefore, blood perfusing the skeletal muscles has the same oncotic pressure as the blood flowing through the pulmonary circulation.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 632–633, 661–664.

questions.stem: According to the sliding theory of muscle contraction, which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Myosin length reduces

options.label: B
options.text: I band becomes wider

options.label: C
options.text: A band remains unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: The interval between Z lines remains the same

questions.solutionHtml:
A band remains unchanged

The A-band contains both thick and thin filaments and is the center of the sarcomere that spans the H zone. During contraction, the H-zone, I-band, the distance between Z-lines, and the distance between M-lines all become smaller. However, the A band's size remains constant during contraction.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 97.
